name: Supply Change Capital
identity_check: Confirmed as Supply Change Capital (supplychange.fund), an early-stage VC investing in technology across the food supply chain, co-founded and run by Managing Partners Noramay Cadena and Shayna Harris. Evidence: the firm's own site and the Substack blog it links to, the PR Newswire Fund I release that names www.supplychange.fund, and SEC Form D filings for Supply Change Capital Fund I LP (CIK 1863949) and Fund II LP (CIK 2064181), where both names appear as Managing Partners. The domain supplychangecapital.com is a parked GoDaddy lander, not the firm. This is a food-system supply chain fund, not a general industrial or logistics fund. It is also not Blue Impact Supply Chain Ventures (a co-investor) and not ProducePay. The One Way Summit label 'Supply chain; Physical AI' matches the supply chain focus. The only 'physical AI' wording found is the Peltier post's 'PhysicalAI'.

thesis_text.value: Invests at pre-seed and seed in B2B technology that works as hidden infrastructure for the food system. It has three themes. Supply chain resilience covers traceability, risk forecasting, manufacturing, logistics and cold chain. Health and nutrition covers food safety and nutrition data. Labor and workforce covers tools, including automation. It leans to software and backs only US-incorporated companies.
thesis_text.snippet: The through-line is infrastructure: the critical systems no one sees but everyone needs, underpinning how food moves, scales, and nourishes.

open_items: supplychange.fund/team/, /thesis/, /submit/ and /press/ returned HTTP 500 (WordPress critical error) on 2026-10-30. The full current team roster and titles could not be read from the site; partners come from blog posts, press releases and Form D.

Fund II: no announcement of size, target or final close found. The Form D filed 2025-11-25 shows $21,588,384 sold to 18 investors, offering 'Indefinite', first sale 2024-11-18. The 2025 Year in Review gives AUM $62M (Fund I + partial Fund II), vintage 2025.

Round amounts not stated in any fetched source for Reveal Foods, Peltier, Loamy, People Science, Cargologik, the Alveo Series A extension or Supply Pay. Peltier's $5.6M figure appears only in database search snippets (CB Insights, VC Backed) and is unverified.

Round stage not stated for Loamy (Jan 2026) or Cargologik (Jun 2025). Loamy filed a Form D on 2026-08-25 for a later equity raise ($8,620,276 sold of $9,896,000; first sale 2026-08-12). Whether Supply Change took part in it is unknown.

invests_in_indian_founders: no statement found. The firm invests only in US-based, US-incorporated companies and says it backs founders from all backgrounds. No India-based portfolio company was found.

No explicit physical AI or robotics thesis on firm pages. The closest are the 'labor automation' vertical, the 2024 ag-robotics research posts (titles only, not read) and the Peltier post's 'PhysicalAI' mention. The One Way Summit 'Physical AI' label is unconfirmed.
HQ country not stated in round sources for Reveal Foods, Peltier, People Science, Cargologik, Alveo, FoodHealth and Celleste Bio (the Celleste release dateline is Tel Aviv and New York).

Earlier Fund I deals (e.g. Kadeya, Tendrel, Robigo, Michroma, FoodReady, Partake Foods) were not researched for round details. 2025 follow-on investments (five, per the 2025 Year in Review) are not itemized beyond Helios AI and FoodHealth.
